bills.title: Common Cents Act
bills.status: Received in the Senate and Read twice and referred to the Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs.
bills.nexus: H.R. 3074 would eliminate the penny, directly affecting the U.S. Mint (a Treasury bureau) and its seigniorage revenue calculations under 31 U.S.C. § 5111. Treasury faces implementation risk around rounding rules for cash transactions and potential seigniorage loss that would need to be reflected in budget projections.

bills.title: Failing Bank Acquisition Fairness Act
bills.status: Received in the Senate and Read twice and referred to the Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs.
bills.nexus: H.R. 6556 directly implicates Treasury's Office of the Comptroller of the Currency and the FDIC's resolution authority under the Federal Deposit Insurance Act, as it would impose new procedural or fairness requirements on the acquisition of failing institutions. Treasury must track this bill because changes to failing-bank acquisition rules affect the speed and cost of orderly resolutions, creating potential systemic risk and fiscal exposure if distressed institutions cannot be transferred to acquirers efficiently.

bills.title: Protecting Privacy in Purchases Act
bills.status: Received in the Senate and Read twice and referred to the Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs.
bills.nexus: H.R. 1181 would restrict the sale or disclosure of consumer firearm and ammunition purchase data, touching on Treasury's Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) and the financial institution reporting framework under the Bank Secrecy Act. Treasury faces implementation risk because the bill could constrain how financial institutions flag, code, or share transaction data that feeds into AML and suspicious activity reporting obligations.

bills.title: A concurrent resolution setting forth the congressional budget for the United States Government for fiscal year 2026 and setting forth the appropriate budgetary levels for fiscal years 2027 through 2035.
bills.status: Committee on the Budget. Ordered to be reported without amendment favorably.
bills.nexus: S.Con.Res. 33 directly shapes the discretionary and mandatory spending ceilings and revenue floors that govern Treasury's borrowing authority, debt limit reconciliation instructions, and overall fiscal posture for FY2026 through FY2035. The Office of Fiscal Projections and the Fiscal Assistant Secretary will need to align cash and debt management strategies with whatever topline levels and reconciliation directives the resolution establishes, and any binding deficit targets create downstream compliance risk for Treasury's financing operations.

bills.title: Servicemembers’ Credit Monitoring Enhancement Act
bills.nexus: S. 2074 would expand free credit monitoring requirements for active-duty servicemembers, directly implicating Treasury's Office of Consumer Policy and its oversight role under the Fair and Accurate Credit Transactions Act framework. The implementation risk centers on potential compliance cost mandates flowing to financial institutions supervised by Treasury-affiliated regulators, and any required interagency coordination with the CFPB on rulemaking.

bills.title: A joint resolution terminating the national emergency declared to impose global tariffs.
bills.nexus: S.J.Res. 88 directly implicates Treasury's role under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act and the broader tariff and trade-finance architecture that Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control and the Office of International Affairs help administer alongside USTR and Commerce. If enacted, termination of the emergency would immediately void the legal predicate for the global tariff regime, creating acute implementation risk around revenue collection, bond market expectations, and any pending trade negotiations premised on that tariff leverage.

bills.title: A joint resolution terminating the national emergency declared to impose duties on articles imported from Brazil.
bills.nexus: S.J.Res. 81 directly implicates Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control and the broader tariff-authority framework insofar as emergency-based duty orders are administered and monitored through Treasury's trade finance and sanctions infrastructure. Termination of the emergency would require Treasury to assess revenue impacts from the duty removal and coordinate with CBP on cessation of collection mechanisms.

bills.title: A joint resolution terminating the national emergency declared to impose duties on articles imported from Canada.
bills.nexus: S.J.Res. 77 directly implicates Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control and CBP revenue functions because the underlying emergency declaration under IEEPA authorizes the tariff measures that generate customs duties collected and administered through Treasury accounts. If the resolution advances and terminates the emergency, Treasury and CBP would face immediate implementation obligations to halt duty collection and process refunds on affected Canadian imports.

bills.title: Enhancing First Response Act
bills.nexus: S. 725 would amend requirements around first-responder communications interoperability, touching the Department of Homeland Security rather than a clear Treasury authority or appropriation. Unless a provision surfaces that affects Treasury's financial intelligence, sanctions coordination, or FinCEN reporting infrastructure tied to emergency response systems, Treasury has no direct equities to flag at this stage.

bills.title: A joint resolution providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule submitted by the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency of the Department of the Treasury relating to the review of applications under the Bank Merger Act.
bills.nexus: S.J.Res. 13 directly nullifies a rule issued by the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency, a Treasury bureau, under its Bank Merger Act review authority. Its enactment as Public Law 119-19 voids that merger review framework and requires OCC to assess whether revised rulemaking or interim guidance is needed to fill the resulting regulatory gap.

bills.title: A joint resolution disapproving the rule submitted by the Bureau of Consumer Financial Protection relating to "Defining Larger Participants of a Market for General-Use Digital Consumer Payment Applications".
bills.nexus: S.J.Res. 28 directly nullifies a CFPB rule under the Congressional Review Act, affecting the Bureau's supervisory authority over nonbank digital payment providers such as large fintech wallet and peer-to-peer payment platforms. Treasury's Office of Consumer Policy and its Financial Stability Oversight Council responsibilities are implicated because voiding the rule removes a federal examination framework for significant payment system participants, creating a regulatory gap and potential prudential risk that FSOC may need to monitor.

bills.title: A joint resolution disapproving the rule submitted by the Bureau of Consumer Financial Protection relating to "Overdraft Lending: Very Large Financial Institutions".
bills.nexus: S.J.Res. 18 nullifies a CFPB rule that would have capped overdraft fees at large banks, directly affecting the Office of Consumer Policy and Treasury's broader financial institution oversight equities. The Congressional Review Act disapproval removes a pending regulatory burden but also signals congressional limits on CFPB rulemaking, which Treasury monitors for systemic revenue and consumer credit market stability implications.

bills.title: A joint resolution terminating the national emergency declared to impose duties on articles imported from Canada.
bills.nexus: S.J.Res. 37 directly implicates Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control and Customs Revenue functions, as terminating the emergency would strip the statutory basis under IEEPA for the Canada tariff orders Treasury and CBP currently administer. If enacted, Treasury faces immediate implementation risk in unwinding duty collection mechanisms and potential refund liability for duties already assessed.

bills.title: A joint resolution providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule submitted by the Internal Revenue Service relating to "Gross Proceeds Reporting by Brokers That Regularly Provide Services Effectuating Digital Asset Sales".
bills.status: Message received in Senate: Returned to the Senate pursuant to the provisions of H.Res. 212.
bills.nexus: S.J.Res. 3 directly targets an IRS rule finalized under Treasury/IRS authority governing broker reporting of digital asset gross proceeds, making it a core concern for the Office of Tax Policy and the IRS. If enacted, the Congressional Review Act disapproval would nullify the rule and bar Treasury from issuing a substantially similar regulation without new statutory authority, creating a significant gap in third-party tax reporting infrastructure for digital assets.

bills.title: An original concurrent resolution setting forth the congressional budget for the United States Government for fiscal year 2025 and setting forth the appropriate budgetary levels for fiscal years 2026 through 2034.
bills.status: Resolution agreed to in Senate with amendments by Yea-Nay Vote. 52 - 48. Record Vote Number: 87. (text: CR S1119-1125)
bills.nexus: S.Con.Res. 7 directly engages the Office of Tax Policy and the Fiscal Assistant Secretary by establishing discretionary and mandatory spending ceilings, revenue floors, and reconciliation instructions that constrain Treasury's debt management authorities and budget execution for FY2025 through FY2034. The resolution's reconciliation directives carry significant implementation risk because they can unlock expedited legislative changes to the tax code and federal borrowing limits that Treasury must be prepared to score, administer, and finance through its debt issuance program.
